dossier.architecture: Low-mass differential elevator/arm and universal vacuum gripper optimized for short coral cycles.

subsystems.drivetrain: Custom swerve retained from 2024 with gearing shifted toward acceleration; maximum perimeter and low-mounted motors improve stability.
subsystems.intake: Collapsing polycarbonate four-bar; floating/slotted upper roller accepts upright coral.
subsystems.transfer: V-shaped powered conveyor centers coral; four-screw removal and shaft couplers provide service access.
subsystems.scoring: Differential continuous belt couples elevator and arm while motors stay low. Suction cup serves coral and algae; custom outer silicone seal and twin piston/scotch-yoke vacuum source.
subsystems.endgame: Simple magnetic tube capture and ratcheted winch; added wider wedges after cage slippage.
subsystems.controls: Tag cameras maintain sight through final placement; published Einstein account explains station-sharing and match adaptations.

versions: Einstein station allocation changed from match 8 onward; this is a tactical evolution, not a new mechanism.
dossier.analysis: Vacuum is a mass-distribution choice here. The lightweight high assembly permits aggressive driving, while the vacuum source and differential belt transfer complexity down to the chassis. Reproducing only the suction cup misses the reason the architecture works. New 1833 design-transfer study: docs/context/1833-reference-2025-1690.md. Historical success does not waive the current no-support/no-turret mandate or certify causal performance.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2025-1690 · Differential arm/elevator motion keeps motors low but couples control
context_documents.body:
# 2025-1690: Differential arm/elevator motion keeps motors low but couples control

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The source describes an efficient floor collector, V-shaped powered centering path and a differential elevator/arm transmission. Equal coordinated belt motion translates the carriage; differential motion changes arm angle while the motors stay low. The retained technical record also describes a custom-sealed suction effector and piston/scotch-yoke vacuum source.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team’s explicit objective is short, fast coral cycles and resistance to defense without excessive sacrifice of algae capability. Keeping arm/elevator drive motors at the base serves low moving mass.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A differential does not eliminate shoulder or elevator effort; it redistributes that demand across shared actuators. Motion limits, current and saturation must be considered in joint space and motor space. The vacuum end effector can reduce exposed gripping hardware, but seal geometry and surface condition become critical. A short-cycle strategy also needs coordinated human-player supply and a path that avoids interference with partners.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test simultaneous lift/rotation near motor limits, vacuum retention on damaged or wet pieces, and recovery after a partially seated coral. Preserve emergency climb acceleration as a high-load exception, not the normal durability baseline.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

context_documents.title: 2025-1690 optimization reference for elite simple architecture
context_documents.body:
## 1690, 2025 WHISPER: compact functional description, coupled mechanics and execution

Primary facts: Orbit credits a closed-belt differential elevator reference and describes floor pickup as a cycle-time choice. Team posts identify pressure feedback and maintenance of an adhesive belt connection. Its championship recap discusses alliance interference and switching a partner to predictable loading-station lanes. A later intake-assist post explains driver-intent conditions and velocity correction. These accounts establish that optimization includes control and traffic management, not only a short mechanism list. They do not show that a differential or vacuum is universally simpler for another team.

1833 transfer analysis: separating moving hardware from actuator location can reduce inertia while creating motor-space coupling and calibration work. A differential should be assessed over simultaneous lift/pivot demands, saturation and failure recovery rather than judged by the number of motors saved. A vacuum can make a gripper visually small while moving complexity into sealing, pressure generation, state sensing and maintenance. Those are valid choices if they improve the whole cycle under the team's resources; they are not free complexity elimination.

For match modeling, faster individual floor pickup does not necessarily produce faster alliance throughput if robots fight over the same accessible pieces or routes. Compare shared supply and traffic policies explicitly. A robot designed to dominate can adopt a lane or temporary complementary assignment without having been designed as a weak support machine. The historical alliance discussion is therefore useful to 1833's elite ceiling even though support-only architecture is prohibited. Reserve time to test driver assistance at speed with realistic errors; a theoretically optimal command that surprises the driver may degrade acquisition. Observe driver workload and repeatability as well as mechanism motion time.

Sources: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/orbit-1690-2025-robot-reveal-whisper/492064 ; https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/orbit-1690-2025-robot-reveal-whisper/492064/68 ; https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/orbit-1690-2025-robot-reveal-whisper/492064/71 ; https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/orbit-1690-2025-robot-reveal-whisper/492064/160 ; https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/orbit-1690-2025-robot-reveal-whisper/492064/225 . Read `agent/robot_packets/2025-1690.json` for the existing technical study and caveats.
